reasons.D: Closest movement: short, stacked declaratives, an 'And then' opener, a first-person 'I set this down plainly', the chatty 'Ask a policeman' aside and piled-up lists all echo the passage's talky, enthusiastic amble.
reasons.C: Has the conversational turns, parentheses and short punchy lines ('Nothing is grand. Everything is right.'), but its ironic, polished, balanced sentences sound more urbane than the passage's breezy, slangy voice.
reasons.B: First person and genteel, but the long, evenly built periodic sentences and the extended gentlewoman simile read as a different, more decorous writer, with none of the passage's exclamation or colloquial bounce.
reasons.A: Plain modern expository prose with an even rhythm, no first person, no exclamations or colloquialisms, and a detached stance; least like the author.
